title: Lone lines at two and three places: the cylinder theorem, the identification with line events, and the obstruction
claim: In tiling worlds of fair three-place contacts on triangular tori, the cylinder cover along a class contradicts only in twists odd on that class relative to every fitting twist. In the four orientation worlds, where each fair coin decides one clause on two places, a lone line along c (exactly one of the cylinders along (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) contradicts) is exactly the line event L(c) of the two-literal shielding theorem, because a contradiction whose cluster has rank two makes every cylinder along an odd class contradict; so their dual pairs are equal on every torus. From the exact counts of TRIPLE-SHIELD-20261023-001A-E001, the identity fails for every tested dual pair of a world in which one coin decides three places (36 three-place and 18 shared-coin pairs on the fresh 3 x 4 and 4 x 4 tori, none related by a symmetry map): the dual-pair identity separates coins that reach two places from coins that reach three, not clause width.
failure_conditions: A cylinder along a class contradicts in a twist that agrees on that class with a fitting twist.
An orientation-world configuration whose lone-line status differs from its line-event status, or a rank-two contradiction that leaves a cylinder along an odd class without a contradiction.
foundation_claim_scope: Twisted fair worlds on triangular and square tori with cylinder covers; exact statements and exact finite counts. Lattices are declared; no space or physics is claimed.

Three controls rejected. Proposition 6 cites the frozen, independently checked experiment. No human or external review
